Objective
To be a key member of the Mission to Seafarers South Australia team, providing welfare services to visiting seafarers while supporting the sustainable development and operation of Mission to Seafarers centres across South Australia.
Based in Port Pirie, the Port Welfare Officers will share responsibility for providing seafarer welfare services, supporting volunteers and committees, coordinating administration, and assisting with the development of services in all South Australian ports, including Port Adelaide,  Port Lincoln, Port Giles, Thevenard, Wallaroo and any future centres established within the state.
The role combines practical seafarer welfare, volunteer coordination, administration, stakeholder engagement and centre development.

Level of Responsibility
The Port Welfare Officers report directly to the Regional Director, Mission to Seafarers Australia.
They work closely with the South Australian Management Committee, local port committees, volunteers, port authorities, shipping agents, churches and other stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of welfare services throughout the state.

The role shares responsibility for:
Day-to-day operation of the Port Pirie Seafarers Centre.
Development and support of Mission to Seafarers activities throughout South Australia.
Volunteer recruitment, training and support.
Administrative and financial management of the South Australian operations.
Regular travel to South Australian ports to visit ships, support volunteers and strengthen relationships with industry partners.

Conditions
The successful applicant will be required to maintain:
Current Driver's Licence.
National Police Check.
Safe Church Communities accreditation (or equivalent).
Working With Children Check (or applicable state screening requirements).
Australian Border Force and Port Security access requirements as required.
Capacity to travel throughout South Australia, including overnight travel where necessary.

About the Role
This position would suit someone who is passionate about improving the welfare of seafarers, enjoys working with volunteers and industry, is highly organised, flexible and self-motivated, and is comfortable working across multiple locations.
The role requires initiative, strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with maritime industry stakeholders while developing sustainable welfare services across regional ports.

Knowledge and Experience
The successful applicant will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with confidence using technology.
A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Xero or similar accounting software, databases, social media and web-based systems is desirable.

Essential Skills and Experience
Office administration experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Experience using accounting software (preferably Xero).
Experience coordinating volunteers or community programs.
Current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
Desirable Skills and Experience
Experience preparing agendas, minutes and financial reports.
Website and social media management.
Marketing and communications experience.
Fundraising and grant administration.
Community development experience.
Understanding of the Mission to Seafarers and the maritime industry.
Experience working with committees or not-for-profit organisations.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Seafarer Welfare
Visit ships and provide welfare support to visiting seafarers.
Coordinate transport, shopping, communications and welfare services.
Supply SIM cards, Wi-Fi access and welfare items.
Assist with emergency welfare situations when required.
Promote compliance with the Maritime Labour Convention welfare provisions.
2. Centre and Port Development
Support the ongoing development of Mission to Seafarers services throughout South Australia.
Assist with establishing and growing welfare activities in new and developing ports.
Identify opportunities to improve facilities and services.
Build relationships with port authorities, shipping agents, terminal operators and industry stakeholders.
Promote awareness of seafarer welfare across the maritime community.
3. Administration
Prepare agendas, reports and committee meeting minutes.
Complete and maintain Australian Border Force documentation.
Maintain registrations, licences and compliance records.
Monitor donations and acknowledge supporters.
Support committee office bearers with administration.
Manage SIM cards, vouchers and foreign currency.
Assist the Regional Director with reporting and projects.
4. Communications and Marketing
Monitor incoming enquiries.
Coordinate communications with volunteers, shipping agents and port stakeholders.
Maintain websites and social media platforms.
Produce promotional material highlighting Mission activities.
Represent Mission to Seafarers at community and industry events.
5. Volunteer Management
Recruit new volunteers across South Australia.
Coordinate induction, training and mentoring.
Maintain volunteer records and compliance.
Coordinate Working With Children Checks, port inductions, First Aid and other required training.
Develop volunteer rosters where applicable.
6. Financial Administration
Assist with day-to-day financial administration.
Process invoices and expenses.
Support budgeting and financial reporting.
Maintain accurate records using Xero or equivalent systems.
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Develop productive relationships with:
Flinders Ports
Shipping agents
Maritime unions
AMSA
Australian Border Force
Port Welfare Committees
Local churches
Community organisations
Government agencies
Represent Mission to Seafarers at meetings and forums as required.
8. Attendance
Attend:
South Australian committee meetings.
National Mission to Seafarers conferences.
Volunteer training events.
Industry meetings and conferences.
Ship visits across South Australian ports.
Other duties as directed by the Regional Director.

Employment Conditions
The position is offered as a job-share arrangement, with two Port Welfare Officers working collaboratively to provide consistent coverage across South Australia.
The combined role is funded at 5Days per week, with flexibility to increase hours through project funding or centre development initiatives.
Regular travel throughout South Australia is an essential component of the role, with a Mission vehicle available where appropriate.
Comprehensive on-the-job training will be provided.
The role would suit someone with several years of workplace experience who enjoys working with people, is comfortable travelling, and wants to make a meaningful contribution to the wellbeing of international seafarers visiting South Australian ports.

result.description:
Position: Cook
Type: Full-time
Employer: The Trustee for Maheshvara Family Trust
Location: Numurkah VIC 3636
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
The Trustee for Maheshvara Family Trust operates a well-established restaurant business in Numurkah, Victoria, specialising in the preparation and service of high-quality meals in a welcoming community setting. Committed to delivering exceptional dining experiences through fresh ingredients, authentic flavours, and consistent standards, the business has built a strong local reputation for reliability and customer satisfaction. Core values centre on integrity, teamwork, food safety, and a genuine passion for hospitality, fostering a supportive and collaborative workplace culture where staff are encouraged to grow, contribute ideas, and take pride in delivering outstanding service to the local community.
About the Position:
This full-time Cook role is vital to the smooth and successful operation of the restaurant, with responsibility for preparing and cooking a variety of menu items to the highest standards of quality, taste, presentation, and food safety. The Cook will work as part of a close-knit kitchen team, contributing to efficient service delivery and helping maintain the business’s reputation for excellence in every dish served.
Key Responsibilities:
Examine ingredients to ensure their quality and suitability before preparation.
Regulate the temperature of ovens, grills, fryers and other cooking equipment.
Prepare and cook meat, poultry, seafood, vegetables, rice, pasta, sauces and other menu items.
Season food during preparation and cooking to achieve the required taste and presentation.
Portion food, arrange dishes and add sauces, garnishes and other finishing elements.
Prepare food to meet customers’ dietary requirements, allergies and special requests.
Follow established recipes, portion-control standards and presentation guidelines.
Monitor food supplies and advise management when ingredients or kitchen items need to be ordered.
Receive and inspect food deliveries and ensure products are properly stored and rotated.
Maintain appropriate stock levels and minimise food spoilage and wastage.
Assist with planning menus and developing new dishes when required.
Prepare ingredients by washing, peeling, cutting, marinating and measuring.
Maintain cleanliness and hygiene across cooking stations, equipment and food-storage areas.
Follow food-safety procedures, including temperature control, date labelling and prevention of cross-contamination.
Train and provide guidance to kitchen assistants and junior kitchen employees where required.
Work closely with chefs, kitchen staff and front-of-house employees to ensure orders are prepared accurately and on time.
Comply with workplace health and safety requirements and report hazards, equipment faults or incidents.
Perform other reasonable kitchen-related duties as directed by the Head Chef or Restaurant Manager.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Commercial Cookery.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in food preparation, cooking techniques, and maintaining kitchen hygiene and food safety standards.
Excellent organisational skills with the ability to work efficiently under pressure and manage multiple tasks.
Good communication and teamwork skills to collaborate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff.
A positive, reliable attitude and commitment to delivering high-quality customer-focused service.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Part Time until September 2026
Position Classification: Enrolled Nurse
Remuneration: $37.83 - $41.1 per hour
Hours Per Week: 32
Located in: Central Coast
Requisition ID: REQ666275
Applications Close: Sunday 26 July 2026 at 11:59pm

Are you a compassionate and motivated Enrolled Nurse looking to build your career in a supportive and collaborative healthcare environment? Central Coast Local Health District (CCLHD) is seeking dedicated nursing professionals who are passionate about delivering high-quality, patient-centred care.

About the Opportunity

As an integral member of our nursing team, you will work under the guidance of Registered Nurses to provide holistic care, support positive patient outcomes, and contribute to a culture of excellence across our health services.

As an Enrolled Nurse, you will play a vital role in supporting patients throughout their healthcare journey. In this role you will:

Deliver compassionate, high-quality nursing care under the guidance of Registered Nurses.

Monitor patient wellbeing, administer medications within scope, and maintain accurate clinical documentation.

Support patients with daily living activities while promoting comfort, dignity and independence.

Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to achieve safe, effective and patient-centred care.

For more information about this role, please view the Position Description 

About You

We are looking for someone who has:

Current AHPRA registration as an Enrolled Nurse (Division 2) with approved qualifications for medication administration, including intravenous medications.

Demonstrated clinical nursing knowledge and skills with a commitment to delivering safe, high-quality patient care.

Strong communication, interpersonal and documentation skills, with confidence using healthcare information systems.

The ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team while effectively prioritising workload in a dynamic environment.

A commitment to evidence-based practice, continuous improvement, and a current valid driver's licence.

Applicants must have current work rights in Australia or be a permanent resident or citizen. Unfortunately, we cannot consider applicants who do not meet this requirement.

Benefits

Work-Life Balance: Enjoy flexible hours and job-sharing options, 17.5% annual leave loading, and paid parental leave.

Financial Benefits: Boost your take-home pay with salary packaging, save on car costs with novated leasing, and access relocation assistance.

Health & Wellbeing: Stay active with discounted gym memberships (Fitness Passport), free flu vaccinations, telehealth support, and confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counselling for you and your family. Plus, access discounted private health insurance.

Career Growth: Advance your career with free professional development courses and secondment opportunities.

Need More Information?
Naomi MacManus
Phone: 0482 804 254
Email: Naomi.McManus@health.nsw.gov.au 

Click here to find out more about applying for this position.

Working for Central Coast Local Health District - NSW Health 

Central Coast Local Health District is committed to implementing the Child Safe Standards.

Central Coast Local Health District is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants can access support through the Stepping Up initiative, which provides guidance on the NSW Health recruitment process. You're also welcome to reach out to Nathan Bramston-Dean in our Aboriginal Workforce Development Team at CCLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au or call 02 4320 3519 for one-on-one support.

Vaccination Requirements

All NSW Health workers are required to comply with the Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination Against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy Directive. This includes:

Category A positions: Mandatory evidence of protection against specified infectious diseases, including annual influenza vaccination and tuberculosis assessment. 

Category B positions: Vaccination is recommended but not mandatory. 
 

Applicants must provide appropriate evidence of compliance prior to commencement. For detailed information, please refer to the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination Policy.

NSW Health strongly recommends all workers stay up to date with COVID-19 vaccinations as per the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation guidelines. However, COVID-19 vaccination is not a condition of employment.

Additional Information

An Eligibility List (E-List) or talent pool may be created from this recruitment episode to assist in filling future permanent, temporary, or casual full-time and part-time positions.

Stay Connected

Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn to stay up to date with career opportunities and the latest updates.

You are encouraged to complete applications on a week day where Technical Support is available Monday to Friday 8.30am to 4.30pm by phoning ROB Help Desk on 1300 679 367.
